Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

entries.title: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
entries.abstract: I present a comprehensive analysis of all publicly available NuSTAR observations of the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (2012--2024). The hard X-ray continuum is well described by thermal Comptonization in a hot corona, with electron temperatures $kT_{\rm e} \approx 40-125$ keV and optical depths $τ\approx 0.4-1.2$ (slab geometry). A clear anti-correlation between $kT_{\rm e}$ and $τ$ is observed, consistent with a thermostat behavior with constant Compton parameter $γ\approx 3.12$ calculated according to Sunyaev and Titarchuk (1980). Variability on timescales of hours constrains the size of the emitting region to $R \approx 250-1200 r_{\rm g}$, corresponding to moderate compactness values $\ell \lesssim 4$. The source occupies the same region of the compactness--temperature plane as other local Seyferts, with no evidence for pair runaway. I then explore two astroparticle implications. The IceCube neutrino excess reported toward NGC 4151 corresponds to $L_ν/L_X \approx 0.3\%$, an energetically negligible contribution that does not alter the observed coronal energy balance. An additional injection of pairs from the hypothetical X17 boson cannot produce significant changes, unless the injection rate exceeds the photoproduction one, but no anomalies were found in the present data set. The NuSTAR data thus provide no evidence for either a significant neutrino cooling channel or an X17-related pair injection in the corona of NGC 4151.

entries.title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
entries.abstract: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

entries.title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
entries.abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. We analyse JCMT/POL-2 maps of nine NGC 1333 regions and ALMA Band 7 maps of two IRAS 4A regions. We estimate plane-of-sky field strengths and derive fluctuation spectra from polarisation-angle structure functions. Where these spectra are sufficiently constrained, we apply quasi-linear gyro-resonant theory to calculate CR pitch-angle scattering rates and $D(E)$. The measured fluctuations constrain CR scattering over proton energy intervals of approximately 0.24-5.3 PeV in NGC 1333 and 10-57 TeV in IRAS 4A. Within these intervals, $D(E)$ spans approximately $3\times10^{28}$-$10^{31}\,{\rm cm^2\,s^{-1}}$. Scattering varies substantially between regions and is stronger where the magnetic-field angular dispersion is greater. Extrapolation to common energies suggests scattering in IRAS 4A is one to two orders of magnitude stronger than its surroundings. Within the directly probed intervals, the scattering mean free paths exceed the individual region sizes. The inferred diffusion coefficients therefore characterise local scattering conditions. A cloud-scale diffusive regime requires CRs to sample multiple regions with different scattering rates. Dust polarisation observations therefore provide constraints on CR scattering in clouds, connecting scattering to cloud-scale transport at energies accessible to $γ$-ray observatories.

entries.title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
entries.abstract: Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. We analyze timing, flux, pulse-profile evolution, and spectra using EP, NICER, and IXPE X-ray observations. Results. We report a 2025 anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586, the largest in this source, with $Δν\approx-1.174(7)\times10^{-7}$ Hz and $Δν/ν\approx-8.19(4)\times10^{-7}$. Unlike its 2019 anti-glitch, this event was radiatively loud: the persistent X-ray flux roughly doubled (~106% increase), followed by a recovery exceeding 320 days. The pulse profile changed modestly but significantly: the valley between the main and secondary peaks became shallower and then recovered with the flux. Spectral properties also changed, and Fermi-GBM detected a short soft gamma-ray burst near the event. These features resemble the radiatively loud 2012 anti-glitch. Conclusions. 1E 2259+586 is unique among magnetars: its anti-glitch rate is comparable to normal spin-up glitch rates, and its anti-glitches can be radiatively loud or relatively quiescent. The fractional anti-glitch amplitudes appear to increase monotonically; further verification is needed. Regular monitoring of 1E 2259+586 is essential for understanding anti-glitch mechanisms.

entries.title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
entries.abstract: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. LMC X-3 exhibits significant changes in both its spectral and timing properties between the two observing campaigns. Hardness-intensity and hardness-rms diagrams reveal a clear separation between the 2024 and 2025 observations and even within the 2024 observations. Overall, it indicates a transition from a relatively harder and more variable state to a brighter, softer, and less variable state. Power spectral analysis shows enhanced broadband variability during the 2024 observations, while the 2025 observations are characterized by weaker variability. Spectral modeling of the combined XSPECT observations indicates an increase in the thermal disk temperature from 0.8 to 1.17 keV, accompanied by a ~5 times increase in X-ray flux between the two epochs. The observed reduction in fractional rms variability with increasing source brightness and decreasing spectral hardness is consistent with more contribution from a stable thermal accretion disk. Taken together, the spectral and timing diagnostics provide a self-consistent picture of accretion-state evolution in LMC X-3, demonstrating the capability of XSPECT to probe long-term variability and accretion processes in bright black hole X-ray binaries.

entries.title: The PAU Survey: Dissecting strong-lensing systems with narrow-band photometric redshifts
entries.abstract: Wide-field imaging surveys such as Euclid will identify large samples of strong-lens candidates, whose scientific use requires redshifts for both deflectors and lensed sources. Source redshifts are challenging because faint arcs are blended with foreground light. We test lens-model-informed photometry on eight known strong lenses, using broad-band models to define component regions, point-reflection subtraction to reduce contamination, and PAU Survey narrow bands combined with five HSC or CFHT broad bands. BCNz estimates separate lens and source redshift distributions without imposing their expected ordering. All eight lens redshift peaks agree with spectroscopy within $|δ_z|\leq0.014$, where $δ_z=(z_b-z_{\rm spec})/(1+z_{\rm spec})$. Four source peaks, all at $z_{\rm s}^{\rm spec}\leq1.23$, agree within $|δ_z|\leq0.025$. Symmetric subtraction reduces the median source $|δ_z|$ from 0.336 to 0.071. At $|δ_z|<0.05$, narrow- plus broad-band photometry yields eight lens and four source matches, versus three and two using EAZY with broad bands alone. These results demonstrate component redshift recovery in blended systems and support redshift-based lens-candidate assessment alongside morphology and colour. Larger narrow-band surveys, including J-PAS, could extend this approach, pending uncertainty calibration and blind candidate tests.

entries.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
entries.abstract: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

entries.title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
entries.abstract: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. Ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) have driven this revolution over the past two decades. In this plenary review, presented at the 9th Heidelberg International Symposium on High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy (Gamma 2026), I provide a synthesis of recent breakthrough physics discoveries achieved by current IACT arrays (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and VERITAS) alongside early scientific achievements from the Large-Sized Telescope prototype (LST-1) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key highlights include the definitive establishment of recurrent novae as transient cosmic-ray proton accelerators via RS Ophiuchi; spatially resolved multi-TeV emission from the relativistic jet termination shocks of microquasars; the discovery of a 20 TeV pulsed radiation component from the Vela pulsar, challenging established magnetospheric emission paradigms; precision measurements of the Galactic Center diffuse ridge spectrum favoring a high-energy cutoff; the detection of distant flat-spectrum radio quasars at $z \sim 1$ (OP 313 and PKS 0346-27), providing tight cosmological constraints on the Extragalactic Background Light; multi-wavelength afterglow detections of $γ$-ray bursts including GRB 221009A; and world-leading joint indirect dark matter limits from dwarf spheroidal galaxy and Galactic Center halo analyses. Together with algorithmic advances in deep learning reconstruction and the ongoing construction of CTAO, these milestones demonstrate the enduring vitality and future trajectory of ground-based $γ$-ray astrophysics.

entries.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
entries.abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $ω_α$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $λ_α$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_α$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

entries.title: Towards a new model of the compact triple system $λ$ Tauri I. Improved periods and preliminary elements of the triple system
entries.abstract: We analysed our new radial velocity measurements and photometric observations (covering a time interval of 46838~days and 39100~days, respectively) as well as those from previous studies to derive accurate ephemerides for both orbits of the compact triple system $λ$ Tau. In the case of the inner eclipsing subsystem, we obtained a~linear ephemeris of T min.I=HJD 2440998.86069(35)+3.952952845(81)xE, improving the accuracy of the previous solutions by more than an order of magnitude. This allowed us to reproduce well all available light curve minima, including the first one recorded in 1844. Furthermore, the period of the outer subsystem, determined from radial velocity analysis, appears to be constant over the interval of available observations, with the corresponding linear ephemeris being T periast.=HJD 2456822.5(3.6)+33.02480(28)xE. Assuming near coplanarity of the inner and outer orbits, we estimated the preliminary physical properties of the whole system. We found that the secondary of the inner subsystem is filling or nearly filling its Roche lobe. We used the long-term stability of the eclipsing subsystem period to place a strong upper limit on the rate of the proposed episodic mass transfer to its primary component. Our results constitute a preparatory step for a follow-up study that will also include an analysis of a rich collection of optical spectro-interferometric observations and use a full-fledged numerical model to describe the evolution of the orbital architecture of the system. Particular attention will be focused on determining the inner orbit forced eccentricity and understanding the absence of the apsidal advance of the outer orbit in our present solution.

entries.title: Shot noise, aperture and resolution in Fourier measurements of disc lopsidedness: TNG50-1 and TNG100-1 analysed with TNGGalaxyLab
entries.abstract: We present TNGGalaxyLab, an open-source Python pipeline for particle-based Fourier decomposition of the stellar surface density of simulated disc galaxies. It measures m = 1-4 amplitude and phase profiles in the Rix and Zaritsky (1995) normalisation, handles IllustrisTNG snapshot conventions, and recovers injected amplitudes in synthetic discs to better than 2 per cent at N = 5 x 10^5. Fourier amplitudes are positive-definite, so Poisson noise biases them upwards by an amount that grows as the particle number falls. We measure a per-galaxy noise floor by randomising particle azimuths and define a noise-corrected amplitude A1,corr. Downsampling TNG50-1 discs to the TNG100-1 particle mass inflates the uncorrected A1 by 40-60 per cent, while A1,corr is recovered to within approximately 10 per cent. We then process all central galaxies with 3.16 x 10^9 < M*/Msun < 10^11 in TNG50-1 (915) and TNG100-1 (6717) with identical settings in the [1.5, 2.5] Rd aperture. Removing the bootstrap and shot-noise biases lowers the TNG100/TNG50 ratio of median A1 from 2.3 to 1.6. At fixed stellar mass, kinematically selected TNG100-1 discs remain 1.5-1.9 times more lopsided after correction; this excess persists whether the aperture is defined in Rd or in kpc, is not explained by kappa_rot or D/T, and is largest at 3.5-6 kpc. TNG50-1 is statistically consistent with the mass-matched S4G sample of Zaritsky et al. (2013); TNG100-1 is not. The low A1 reported for TNG100 by Lokas (2022) cannot be read as a resolution deficit, since with matched measurements TNG100-1 is more lopsided than TNG50-1. Code and catalogues are public.

entries.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
entries.abstract: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

entries.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
entries.abstract: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

entries.title: Tracing the Epoch of Reionization through extreme emission line galaxies around Cosmic Noon
entries.abstract: Star-forming galaxies at z>6 are thought to be the main drivers of cosmic reionization, but their faintness makes detailed study challenging even with JWST. Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems with intense nebular emission and are potential lower-redshift analogues of this population. We aim to assemble and characterize a statistically significant sample of EELGs in the CANDELS/EGS field around cosmic noon, and to assess their validity as analogues of the galaxies that drove reionization. We select EELG candidates from CANDELS photometry with a J-band color-excess criterion that identifies both H$β$+[OIII] and H$α$ emitters. Physical properties are taken from CANDELS data products, and the selection is validated with MMT/MMIRS, Keck/MOSFIRE, HST/WFC3 and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, complemented by our own GTC/OSIRIS+ program. We identify 102 H$β$+[OIII] emitters at $z\sim1.7$ and 127 H$α$ emitters at $z\sim1.0$. They are compact ($\sim$1.6 kpc), low-mass ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim8$) and strongly star-forming (sSFR $\sim10^{-8}$ yr$^{-1}$). Estimated purities of $84.3\pm1.5$\% (H$β$+[OIII]) and $76.8\pm2.0$\% (H$α$) agree with spectroscopic confirmation rates (85\% and 63\%), with no evidence of significant AGN contamination. A joint Bayesian fit, corrected for completeness via a truncated likelihood, yields $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) = (6.71\pm0.16) + (3.31\pm0.46)\log(1+z)$, suggesting an evolution in the characteristic mass of the sample with cosmic time. We spectroscopically confirm a highly pure, AGN-free sample of cosmic-noon EELGs. While their mass scale evolves with redshift, their properties consistently match those of z>5 JWST extreme emitters, supporting them as intermediate-redshift analogues.

entries.title: Constraining electron heat flux from reduced measurements
entries.abstract: Coronal heating estimates depend partly on electron heat transport. Different electron velocity distributions can match the same observations yet carry different heat fluxes. We ask which measurements are enough to determine heat flux without finding how electrons are distributed across all speeds and directions. The solar wind carries electrons outward from the corona and allows their velocities to be measured directly. Using one Wind measurement, we keep density, mean flow, temperature and angular summaries for each energy channel. In the fixed-bin model, electron distributions that match these quantities have heat fluxes from 3.58 to 19.85 $μ$W m$^{-2}$. Keeping the correlation between electron motion along and across the magnetic field fixes the heat flux at 11.73 $μ$W m$^{-2}$, matching the original bin calculation. This recovers heat flux without reconstructing the full shape of the electron velocity distribution. When the measured counts vary, retaining the required correlations leaves the same heat-flux range as direct calculation from those counts. We propose testing coronal observations in the same way to find which features of electron motion they constrain well enough to determine heat transport. Those constraints could help establish the heating requirements used to assess coronal heating mechanisms.

entries.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
entries.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

entries.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
entries.abstract: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

entries.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
entries.abstract: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

entries.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
entries.abstract: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$α$ and Pa$α$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$α$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,μ{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

entries.title: A Statistical Analysis of Lopsidedness in Disk Galaxies
entries.abstract: We present a statistical analysis of Fourier lopsidedness in disk galaxies based on a deduplicated compilation of 606 unique objects: 442 have a measured m = 1 amplitude (A1), and 302 of these also have a measured m = 2 amplitude (A2), with no entry carrying A2 alone. The sample is a factor of approximately 3 larger than earlier homogeneous A1-A2 datasets. Our main results are: (i) Both A1 and A2 follow log-normal distributions (KS D = 0.046 and 0.048) which are strongly preferred over Rayleigh or exponential forms, pointing to a multiplicative amplification process rather than random-phase superposition. (ii) The m = 1 and m = 2 modes are correlated as A2 = 0.29 A1 + 0.11 (Spearman rho = 0.501, p less than 10^-19). (iii) A1 rises monotonically with morphological T-type from approximately 0.07 in E/S0 to approximately 0.37 in Sm/Im galaxies (Kendall tau = 0.234, p approximately 10^-12). (iv) A1 anti-correlates with gas rotation velocity (Spearman rho = -0.432) and, in a stellar-mass cross-matched subsample of 246 galaxies with independent stellar-mass estimates, with stellar mass (rho = -0.395). The weaker lopsidedness of massive, fast-rotating disks indicates that the observed m = 1 amplitude is regulated by internal dynamics rather than set by tidal perturbations alone. (v) The TNG50-1 simulation, analysed through the TNGGalaxyLab Fourier pipeline, reproduces the observed A1-stellar-mass anti-correlation with a nearly identical Spearman coefficient, although its median A1 is approximately 1.4 times lower, an offset consistent with the heterogeneous target selection of the observational compilation.

entries.title: Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies
entries.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.

entries.title: Revisiting the centrifugal breakout scaling relationship for H$α$ emission in light of $ρ$ Oph C, the coolest B-type star with an H$α$-bright centrifugal magnetosphere
entries.abstract: The corotating magnetospheres of B-type stars are strongly affected by magnetic field strength and rotational velocity, which determine both the geometry and strength of visible and radio emission; however, H$α$ emission largely disappears below a bolometric luminosity of $\log{(L / L_\odot)} \sim 2.8$. The nearby B5 V star $ρ$ Oph C (HD 147932) is the least-luminous rapidly rotating magnetic B-type star to display magnetospheric H$α$ emission. While $ρ$ Oph C's radio magnetosphere has been extensively studied, its magnetic field and H$α$ magnetosphere have been constrained only via snapshot observations. We present a new dataset of high-resolution ESPaDOnS spectropolarimetry covering the star's rotational period, which is revisited by combining Hipparcos, K2 and TESS photometry. We find that the star's magnetic field strength and geometry are consistent with the model inferred from radio data. As expected from the magnetic model, there is very little variability in H$α$. Comparison of the light curve to both equivalent width measurements from metallic lines and magnetospheric models suggests that the star's photometric variability is dominated by surface chemical abundance spots; however, there is complex rotationally modulated variability at about the mmag level which probably originates in the magnetosphere. $ρ$ Oph C is the least luminous B-type star in which magnetospheric H$α$ emission has yet been detected, and its emission is notably weaker than the predictions of the centrifugal breakout model. Its photometric eclipse depth is also much lower than predicted by the CBO model. However, its radio luminosity is consistent with CBO predictions. We speculate on this basis that $ρ$ Oph C may be a transitional object between effective temperature regimes with hydrogen-dominated and decoupled metallic winds.

entries.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
entries.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

analysis.result: In all three scenarios the Circinus Galaxy is by far the brightest southern Seyfert in both neutrinos and MeV $\gamma$-rays. analysis.reason: This Swift-XRT population study separates early–narrow and late–wide GRB X-ray flares and tests prolonged accretion against external-shock variability, directly constraining compact-object central engines and relativistic outflows.
analysis.result: A rest-frame GMM of $(t_{\rm pk},w)$ yields two populations: early–narrow (~80%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{2}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\lesssim1$; center $\log_{10}(t_{\rm pk},w)=(1.97,1.85)$) and late–wide (~20%, $\langle t_{\rm pk}\rangle\simeq10^{3.5}\,{\rm s}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\gtrsim2$; center $(3.49,3.80)$). Their mean energies are consistent, $\langle\log_{10}(E_{\rm iso,f,rest})\rangle=51.13\pm0.10$ versus $50.66\pm0.20$ (K–S $p=0.22$). Early–narrow flares follow $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}\propto t_{\rm pk,rest}^{-1.74^{+0.24}_{-0.24}}$, while late–wide flares give $-0.19^{+1.01}_{-0.93}$; the combined slope is $-1.60^{+0.12}_{-0.12}$, shallower than $L_{\rm pk}\propto t_{\rm pk}^{-3}$. The global fit $\log w_{\rm rest}=\alpha+\beta\log t_{\rm pk,rest}$ has $\beta=1.21^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$, but only early–narrow flares are significant ($\beta=1.04^{+0.12}_{-0.13}$, $w/t_{\rm pk}\sim0.76$ versus $\sim2.04$). Waiting times are $\sim76\,{\rm s}$ versus $\sim2950\,{\rm s}$.

analysis.problem: The origin of GRB X-ray flares is unresolved: they may be prolonged central-engine activity or external-shock variability, and it is unclear whether one temporal scaling describes all flares.
analysis.method: Light curves from 100 redshift-known Swift-BAT GRBs (89 fitted; 61 with flares) are modeled with asymmetric Norris profiles. Rest-frame $t_{\rm pk}$, $w$, asymmetry, and $E_{\rm iso,f}$ adopt flat $\Lambda$CDM with $\Omega_{\rm m}=0.286$ and $H_0=70\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. A multivariate GMM classifies $(t_{\rm pk},w)$; K–S, Spearman, and Bayesian regression test relations. Luminosity is $L_{\rm avg,f,rest}=E_{\rm iso,f,rest}/w_{\rm rest}$, and accretion timing is compared with $t_{\rm visc}\sim\alpha^{-1}(H/R)^{-2}\Omega_K^{-1}$.
assumptions: Fallback material circularizes and then accretes on the viscous time $t_{\rm visc}\sim\alpha^{-1}(H/R)^{-2}\Omega_K^{-1}$.
limits: Broad flares can be absorbed into empirical power-law afterglow segments, and 11 bursts with extremely large fitted widths were excluded.

The dashed lines show the median Bayesian linear regression obtained with LinMix, while the faint lines represent random posterior realizations of the fitted relation. A statistically significant anti-correlation is found for the early–narrow flares, whereas no significant trend is detected for the late–wide population. Because the average flare luminosity is not identical to the instantaneous jet luminosity, this relation provides only an indirect comparison with the luminosity evolution predicted by accretion-powered central-engine models. The black dashed line represents the Bayesian regression fitted to the individual flare measurements, with $\beta=-1.60\pm 0.12$, while the blue solid line shows the separate fit to the binned geometric mean luminosities, yielding $\beta=-1.65^{+0.24}_{-0.20}$. figures.caption: Figure 4: Relation between the rest-frame flare peak time, $t_{\rm pk,rest}$, and the flare isotropic energy, $E_{\rm iso,f,rest}$ (left), and between the rest-frame flare width, $w_{\rm rest}$, and $E_{\rm iso,f,rest}$ (right). The purple and green points represent the early–narrow (Cluster 0; 78 flares) and late–wide (Cluster 1; 19 flares) flare populations, respectively. The error bars correspond to the $1\sigma$ uncertainties. The dashed lines show the median Bayesian linear regressions obtained using the method of Kelly [25], which accounts for measurement uncertainties in both variables as well as intrinsic scatter. For the $t_{\rm pk,rest}$ – $E_{\rm iso,f,rest}$ relation, we obtain $\beta=-0.14^{+0.05}_{-0.06}$ ($\alpha=9.3^{+2.8}_{-2.4}$) for the early–narrow flares and $\beta=0.05^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$ ($\alpha=1.1^{+3.5}_{-3.7}$) for the late–wide flares. analysis.result: VLT spectra identify optical C IV $\lambda\lambda 5801,5812$ (C IV $\lambda 5805$) in off-nuclear TDE 2025abcr, at a projected offset of $9.3\,\mathrm{kpc}$ and $z\simeq 0.05$. The proposed excitation is continuum fluorescence plus photon trapping in the $312\,\mathrm{\AA}$ transition, analogous to WN winds and requiring strong EUV irradiation and high optical depth. A single-temperature fit gives $T_{\mathrm{BB}}\simeq 2\times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}$, below $3\times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{K}$ from the UV plus blue optical; the lack of rapid variability implies a reprocessing photosphere with $R\sim 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$. Broad-line widths are relatively narrow, $\sim 2500$–$3000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, while He II and N III FWHM decline from $\sim 4000$–$5000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $\sim 2000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Peak luminosity suggests $M_{\mathrm{BH}}\sim 10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$ with large uncertainty, and Swift/XRT detects $L_{X}\sim 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.3$–$10\,\mathrm{keV}$) without intrinsic absorption.
analysis.problem: The paper asks whether the feature near $5805\,\mathrm{\AA}$ in off-nuclear TDE 2025abcr is optical C IV $\lambda\lambda 5801,5812$, rather than shifted He I or [N II], and what its excitation implies for a compact, dense reprocessing region.
analysis.method: The analysis combines ZTF forced-PSF and LCOGT difference-imaging photometry, GTC/HiPERCAM and LCOGT intranight monitoring, and Swift/XRT–UVOT data with six VLT/FORS2 spectra ($R\simeq 900$) and one NOT/ALFOSC spectrum ($R\sim 300$), calibrated to contemporaneous photometry and corrected for $E(B-V)=0.013\,\mathrm{mag}$. A flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology is adopted, the continuum is fit by a single-temperature blackbody, and each line by concentric double-Lorentzian components. Non-variability at the $0.008\,\mathrm{mag}$ ($g$) and $0.025\,\mathrm{mag}$ ($u$) levels is used to infer $R\sim 10^{14}\,\mathrm{cm}$.
assumptions: The absence of rapid variability is interpreted as emission from an extended, reprocessing-dominated optical photosphere.

analysis.result: With an effective livetime of $10.6$ yr ($25.9$ station-years after quality cuts), no neutrino candidate remains. The single phased-array event ($\mathrm{SNR}\sim 12$, elevation $-35^\circ$) is local A5 detector emission. The expected background is $0.13\pm 0.01\,(\mathrm{stat.})^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\,(\mathrm{syst.})$, from $b_{\mathrm{surf}}=4.50^{+1.01}_{-0.85}\times 10^{-2}$ and $b_{\mathrm{therm}}=8.65^{+0.44}_{-0.28}\times 10^{-2}$, giving a $5\sigma$ threshold $n_{\mathrm{disc}}=4$. Analysis efficiency is $28\%$ for a flux at current experimental upper limits. The $90\%$ CL all-flavor limit is the strongest reported at $50$–$1000\,\mathrm{EeV}$ and excludes the Muzio trans-GZK model. Analysis-level expectations are Global UL $5.3$ ($\epsilon=27.6\%$), Muzio $2.4$ ($21.8\%$), Kotera $0.4$ ($21.1\%$), $100\%$ protons $0.2$ ($25.0\%$), Fang pulsars $0.2$ ($16.7\%$), and KM3NeT $1.6$ ($13.8\%$).
analysis.problem:
Whether a diffuse flux of ultrahigh-energy neutrinos, $E_
u\gtrsim 100\,\mathrm{PeV}$, including cosmogenic neutrinos from UHECR interactions with the CMB and EBL, is detectable through in-ice Askaryan radio pulses. UHECRs ($E_{\mathrm{CR}}\gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{EeV}$) are mostly extragalactic heavy nuclei whose magnetic deflections block source tracing, while protons are GZK-suppressed above $\sim 10^{19.7}\,\mathrm{eV}$; near $1\,\mathrm{EeV}$, IceCube and ANITA give $E_
u^2\Phi_
u\lesssim 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{GeV}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}\,\mathrm{sr}^{-1}$.
analysis.method: Five ARA stations (2013–2023) are analyzed with $10\%$ of data for background design and $90\%$ blinded. NuLeptonSim generates $E^{-1}$ neutrinos from $10^{16}$–$10^{21}\,\mathrm{eV}$ for later reweighting inside a fiducial cylinder, using Connolly cross sections and PREM; AraSim models the stations. AraProc22 calibrates waveforms and applies a $50$–$875\,\mathrm{MHz}$ bandpass. Signal strength is $\mathrm{SNR}=(V_{\mathrm{pp}}/2)/\mathrm{RMS}$. Direction uses $C_{ij}(\tau)$ with $n(z)=n_{\mathrm{ice}}-(n_{\mathrm{ice}}-n_{\mathrm{firn}})e^{-z/\Lambda}$ ($n_{\mathrm{ice}}=1.780$, $n_{\mathrm{firn}}=1.326$, $\Lambda\simeq 49.505\,\mathrm{m}$). Phased-array beams scale as signal $\propto N$ and noise $\propto\sqrt{N}$. Cuts minimize the $5\sigma$ discovery normalization at $E_0=10^{18.5}\,\mathrm{eV}$, $$\phi_0^{\mathrm{disc}}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma},\boldsymbol{\Theta})=\frac{\mathrm{FC}(n_{\mathrm{disc}}(B),B)}{\int f(E)\,\mathcal{E}(E)\,dE}.$$ Thermal separation uses impulsivity $\mathcal{I}=2\langle H\rangle-1$.

analysis.reason: This paper quantitatively tests whether atomic and molecular line photons, inverse-Compton scattered in a relativistic outflow, can produce the evolving MeV feature of GRB 221009A, a direct constraint on jet radiation and dense circumstellar or molecular seed supply.
analysis.result: No line-seed inverse-Compton candidate is shown to satisfy photon supply, relative components, LAT consistency, and escape together. In the observer-directed Thomson limit, $\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}\simeq 2\gamma_e^2\epsilon(1-\beta_e\mu_i)/(1+z)$, while a head-on collision approaches $4\gamma_e^2\epsilon/(1+z)$. For host-frame $Ly\alpha\simeq 10.2\,{\rm eV}$ and $H\alpha\simeq 1.89\,{\rm eV}$, scattering to $10\,{\rm MeV}$ needs $\gamma_{e,Ly\alpha}\simeq 531$ and $\gamma_{e,H\alpha}\simeq 1.23\times 10^3$. A log-normal electron distribution seeded by H$_2$ $2.122\,\mu{\rm m}$ ($0.584\,{\rm eV}$) matches two published intervals at $E_{\rm c,H_2}=11.5$ and $8.8\,{\rm MeV}$, with $\gamma_0=3.30\times 10^3$ and $2.69\times 10^3$ and $s_\gamma=0.087$ and $0.177$; the corresponding trial UV centroids are about $210$ and $161\,{\rm MeV}$ with standard deviations about $35$ and $55\,{\rm MeV}$. None of 40 molecular combinations lies below the adopted central envelope at all sampled energies, and trace minima are about $3.46$, $1.48$, $1.60$, and $1.40$. Even under ideal excitation and internal escape, compact reference-line densities fall short by factors of approximately $4$–$9$; precursor-assisted deficits remain at least about $4.3$, or about $87$–$1.7\times 10^2$ for single photon use. A decreasing centroid does not uniquely imply electron deceleration, and the four-interval calibration $\gamma_0\simeq(3.30,2.70,1.62,2.08)\times 10^3$ is non-monotonic.

analysis.problem: Can H$_2$ ultraviolet-fluorescence photons, hydrogen recombination lines, or metal K-shell lines, scattered once by relativistic electrons, explain the Fermi-GBM MeV feature of GRB 221009A without violating the simultaneous LAT spectrum, local photon supply, timing, angular geometry, and the adopted spectral envelope?
analysis.method: The model uses anisotropic single-scattering kinematics and a Klein–Nishina emissivity. With recoil parameter $b\equiv 4\gamma_e\epsilon/(m_ec^2)$, the local response is $d\ln\epsilon^{\rm IC}_{\rm obs}/d\ln\epsilon=1/(1+b)$. The flux is $F_{\epsilon_{\rm obs}}(\epsilon_{\rm obs},t_{\rm obs})=\frac{1+z}{d_L^2}\int d^3\boldsymbol{r}\,j_{\rm IC}[(1+z)\epsilon_{\rm obs},\Omega_{\rm s},\boldsymbol{r},t_{\rm ret}]e^{-\tau_{\rm esc}}$, integrated on equal-arrival-time surfaces with $dt_{\rm obs}=(1+z)(1-\beta_e\mu_{\rm s})dt$. Electrons follow $\frac{dN_e}{d\ln\gamma_e}=\frac{N_e}{\sqrt{2\pi}s_\gamma}\exp\left[-\frac{(\ln\gamma_e-\ln\gamma_0)^2}{2s_\gamma^2}\right]$; $\gamma_0$ and $s_\gamma$ are calibrated to photon moments, and 40 PDR-template plus external-screen combinations are compared with reconstructed central spectra. Optically thin component ratios scale as $\frac{F_{2,B_2}}{F_{1,B_1}}=\frac{u_2}{u_1}\frac{\mathcal{P}_{2,B_2}}{\mathcal{P}_{1,B_1}}$.
assumptions: Ideal excitation and internal escape are assumed when estimating the compact reference-line photon density.
Hydrogen recombination-line gas is first taken at rest in the host frame and requires a suitably directed radiation field at the scattering site.
limits: None of the 40 molecular combinations satisfies the baseline central spectral envelope at all sampled energies, and the comparison is not a statistical exclusion.
Compact examples remain short of the required reference-line photon density by factors of approximately 4–9, and no calculated geometry closes the molecular photon, timing, and angular budgets.
Moment matching does not reproduce the full line profile; the non-monotonic gamma0 sequence is not a joint posterior and is not evidence of cooling.
